title: SymADiT: Symmetry-Aware Crystal Generation with Latent Flow Matching
claim: A two-stage pipeline first learns a structure-aware latent space by reconstruction, then generates new samples by flow matching in that space.
layout: 2 rows, left-to-right, stage titles above each row, flow-matching inset
description: A two-row block diagram. Row 1, labeled 'Stage 1: Autoencoder for reconstruction', goes left to right. A crystal lattice image feeds a gray 'Symmetry-Aware Crystal Representation' box. That box goes through a cyan trapezoid Encoder, then a green 'Latent Representation' box, then a cyan Decoder. The Decoder outputs another gray representation box and a reconstructed crystal image. Row 2, labeled 'Stage 2: Latent flow matching', starts with 'Random Gaussian Noise' on the left. An arrow leads into a flow-field inset: pink streamlines run from a Gaussian-like distribution to a multimodal one, with a green noisy trajectory drawn over them. Below the inset is the caption 'Denoising with Diffusion Transformer'. The row then continues to a green 'Sampled Latent Representation' box, a cyan Decoder, and a final crystal structure image. Gray, green and cyan boxes are used consistently for data and modules. Arrows are thick and gray.
caption: Illustration of our representation and framework, which is inspired by ADiT [ref]: Training an autoencoder for reconstruction, followed by learning a generative model over its latent representations. However, in our approach, the decoded representation explicitly contains symmetry information, thus enabling the generation of crystals with realistic symmetry properties by design.
abstract: Tackling the task of crystal generation, we aim to enhance the previously proposed, symmetry-agnostic, All-atom Diffusion Transformer (ADiT) by introducing SymADiT, a symmetry-aware variant. To do so, we use a representation of crystals based on Wyckoff positions. We follow ADiT and perform generative modelling in latent space, adapted to our symmetry-aware representation. By forcing the output of the generative model to adhere to the symmetry restrictions imposed by the generated crystal's space group and each atom's Wyckoff position, the generated crystals exhibit more realistic symmetry properties. We benchmark our method against both symmetry-aware and symmetry-agnostic models for crystal generation and show competitive performance, generating stable, symmetric, and physically plausible crystals with only an off-the-shelf Transformer architecture. Our code is available at https://github.com/Karmush21/SymADiT.
